nodes.summary: For natural numbers $i$ and $n$, this is the list of booleans $(b_0, \dots, b_{n-1})$ of length $n$ in which $b_k$ is true exactly when $\lfloor i / 2^k \rfloor$ is odd: the $n$ lowest binary digits of $i$, least significant bit first.
nodes.title: Lowest $n$ bits of a number, least significant first

nodes.summary: A list of booleans $(b_0, \dots, b_{m-1})$ represents the natural number $\sum_{k < m} [b_k]\, 2^k$, where $[b_k]$ is $1$ if $b_k$ is true and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Value of a list of bits, least significant first

nodes.summary: Let $C = (g_0, \dots, g_{m-1})$ be a list of gates, each encoded as a (kind, references) pair, let $\alpha$ be a list of booleans and let $n$ be a natural number. The gate values of $C$ on $\alpha$ are the values $(v_0, \dots, v_{m-1})$ of the flat Boolean circuit on $n + 2$ inputs obtained by decoding every $g_j$, when input $i$ is given entry $i$ of $\alpha$, read as false when $i$ is at least the length of…
nodes.title: Gate values of an encoded circuit

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a list of $m$ gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs, let $\alpha$ be a list of booleans and let $k$ and $n$ be natural numbers. The last $k$ outputs of $C$ on $\alpha$ are the last $k$ of the gate values $(v_0, \dots, v_{m-1})$ of $C$ on $\alpha$ as a circuit on $n + 2$ inputs, that is $(v_{m-k}, \dots, v_{m-1})$; when $k > m$ they are all $m$ gate values.
nodes.title: Outputs of an encoded circuit

nodes.summary: An encoded gate is a pair $(k, r)$ of a natural number $k$, the kind of the gate, and a list $r$ of natural numbers, its references. This is the (kind, references) encoding of the gates of a flat Boolean circuit.
nodes.title: Encoded gates

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a list of gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs and let $n$ and $j$ be natural numbers. Gate $j$ of $C$ is valid when $C$ has more than $j$ entries and its entry $j$ (counting from $0$) is one of: $(0, [i])$ with $i < n + 2$ (an input gate); $(1, [b])$ with $b \le 1$ (a constant gate); $(2, [a])$ with $a < j$ (a negation gate); or $(3, r)$ or $(4, r)$ where every entry $a$ of $r$ satisfies $a < j$ (a…
nodes.title: Valid gates of a succinct 3SAT descriptor

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a list of gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs and let $n$ be a natural number. The descriptor $C$ is well-formed for $n$ when $C$ has at least $n + 1$ gates, every gate of $C$ is valid for $n$, and the flat Boolean circuit on $n + 2$ inputs obtained by decoding every gate of $C$ is well-formed.
nodes.title: Well-formed succinct 3SAT descriptors

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a list of gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs, let $n$ and $i$ be natural numbers, and let $\sigma$ assign a boolean to every natural number. Clause $i$ of the formula described by $C$ for $n$ is satisfied by $\sigma$ when, for some $j < 3$, literal $j$ of clause $i$ of that formula is a pair $(v, s)$ with $\sigma(v) = s$.
nodes.title: Satisfied clauses of a succinctly described formula

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a list of gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs and let $n$, $i$ and $j$ be natural numbers. Give $C$, as a circuit on $n + 2$ inputs, the input consisting of the $n$ lowest bits of $i$ followed by the $2$ lowest bits of $j$, each least significant bit first, and let $(o_0, \dots, o_{p-1})$ be its last $n + 1$ outputs. nodes.title: Literals of a succinctly described formula

nodes.summary: Succinct 3SAT is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a pair $(n, C)$ of a natural number $n$ and a list $C$ of gates encoded as (kind, references) pairs such that $C$ is a well-formed descriptor for $n$ and some assignment $\sigma$ of booleans to the natural numbers satisfies clause $c$ of the formula described by $C$ for every…
nodes.title: Succinct 3SAT

nodes.summary: The succinct 3SAT decision problem lies in NEXP, and every decision problem in NEXP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: Succinct 3SAT is NEXP-complete

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
